summary: The video is one scan-time pipeline driven by a single H/V counter pair. Background tiles, column scroll, sprite attributes and the big sprite are all fetched in fixed x_pixel phases, sprites go into a line buffer during horizontal blank, and the CPU's VRAM accesses are interleaved into the spare phases. None of MAME's tilemap callbacks, the draw_sprites loop or the screen_update draw order appear. Several quirks MAME handles in software are done here through address wiring or a shared adder, the way a board would do them. The core is not split up per chip and does not use board net names, so this is a hand-made hardware-style design rather than a clear schematic transcription.

findings.note: All the timing signals come straight from bits of hcnt and vcnt: cpu_clock = not hcnt(0), is_sprite = not hcnt(8), sprite = hcnt(6:4), x_tile/x_pixel = hcnt(7:3)/(2:0). The 384x264 raster runs from counters that reload at 128 and 248, rather than from a per-frame callback.

findings.signal: time-shared color RAM / tile RAM addressing per pixel phase
findings.note: The color RAM address is muxed by x_pixel. Phases 000/010/100/110 fetch column scroll, background color and the four sprite bytes (sprite & "10"/"01"/"00"/"11"). The odd phases hand the RAM to the CPU, the way video and CPU share a RAM bus on a board.

findings.signal: sprite line buffer filled during hblank
findings.note: Sprites are drawn into a 256x6 line RAM while hcnt<256 (the blanking half) and are read back and cleared on the next active line, with a pen != 0 sprite-over-background mux. MAME instead loops offs=0x1c..0 and calls gfx->transpen into a frame bitmap.

findings.signal: shared scroll/sprite-Y adder and range test
findings.note: One adder, y_line + y_sp_bg + 1, serves both background column scroll and sprite Y. A sprite counts as on the line when the sum's top nibble is 1111, which is a hardware comparator, not MAME's 240-y screen placement.

findings.signal: flip-Y as address XOR on ROM lines
findings.note: Sprite flips XOR the graphics ROM address bits (y3, x_tile0, y2..0) with "01000"/"10111"/"11111", and background flip-Y inverts y(2:0). MAME expresses the paired-character flip through tile_index ^ 0x20 and TILE_FLIPYX.

findings.signal: color RAM A5 behavior via address wiring
findings.note: The background color is addressed as '1' & y_line_shift(7:4) & x_tile, so the RAM is simply not indexed by that row bit. MAME instead writes the byte twice (offset & ~0x20 and | 0x20).

findings.signal: big sprite as counter plus fine-shift delay line
findings.note: The big sprite is drawn from an x counter preset to 120+(x and F8), a 16x16 map indexed by counter bits (6:3), and an 8-bit shift-register delay that takes the fine x(2:0) offset. It is clipped by y_shift(7) and an x-counter window. MAME uses a 32x32 tilemap with scroll and a transmask group for the lower-right quadrant.

findings.signal: NMI latched from raster line, masked by latch bit
findings.note: A flip-flop sets NMI when y_tile=11100 and y_pixel=000, and is held cleared by a latch bit decoded from writes to A000 with A2..0=000 (LS259-style). This comes from the board's counters, not from a screen_vblank callback.
video_mux always puts the big sprite on top, and 98DC is never latched. This is a simplification. It does not follow MAME's draw order, and it is not a board PROM priority either.

The address decode matches the board map (8000 RAM, 8800 big sprite RAM, 9000 video RAM, 98xx, A000-B800 ports), as any correct core must. Decoding uses 2K address blocks, and nothing is organized around MAME's region names.

Everything specific to this board sits in one entity, with descriptive names (x_tile, is_sprite, attr_sp_bg) rather than chip or net names. Only video_gen, the sound block and the palette PROMs are separate modules. This points neither toward board structure nor toward MAME.
The palettes are byte-wide ROMs whose output goes straight to 3-3-2 RGB pins, like PROMs feeding a resistor DAC. MAME's compute_resistor_weights is not reproduced.
